Shri Arun Sharma- learned Counsel for respondents No. 1   WITH  MISC. APPEAL No. 3402 of 2018  SMT. RENU AND OTHERS  Versus  JAGDISH AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Shri Arun Sharma-learned Counsel for appellants- claimants.
 Shri Narendra Singh Tomar- learned Counsel for respondent No  ORDER
Both miscellaneous appeals arise out of a common Award dated 10th April 2018 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT), Gwalior, in Claim Case No. 732 of 2016.

The Insurance Company has filed Misc. Appeal No. 3351 of 2018 under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 (hereinafter referred to as "MV Act"), challenging the compensation amount awarded and asserting contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
Conversely, the claimants have filed Misc. Appeal No. 3402 of 2018, seeking an enhancement in the compensation amount.

2. Necessary facts giving rise to the present appeals, in short, are that the claimants filed a claim petition asserting that the deceased, Dr. Anil Kumar Dwivedi, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:904 2 MA-3351-2018 was traveling with one Shivam Tiwari in his Swift car (No.
DL 2C AP 6868) from Urai to his village Kharela on 31st July 2017.

At Kumharia, the Bolero Pick-up Smt. Renu vs Jagdish on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146692860/
1 (No. UP 95 T 0654), driven rashly and negligently by the driver, collided head-on with the deceased's Swift car, causing his death during subsequent treatment at CSC Raath.

sentences.text: The claimants sought compensation for the loss of the deceased's life.

The Insurance Company, along with the owner and driver of the Bolero vehicle, denied the accident's occurrence as described by the claimants, claiming that the accident was due to the deceased's own negligence.
The Insurance Company raised the issue of contributory negligence, alleging that the deceased's own rash driving caused the head-on collision.
3. It is contended on behalf of the Insurance Company that the accident was caused by the contributory negligence of the deceased.
The deceased was driving his Swift car rashly and negligently, and as such, the claimants are not entitled to the full compensation amount.
The Claims Tribunal wrongly relied on the testimony of an eye- witness, Bharat Kumar Tiwari (PW-3), whose evidence was inconsistent in his statement and a relative of the claimants.
The spot map shows the accident location on a straight road, which should have been interpreted to support the claim of the deceased's negligence.
The income of the deceased was exaggerated and should be assessed at a lower figure.
Furthermore, the future prospects of the deceased were overestimated, given his temporary employment.

In support of their contentions, the Insurance Company has relied on the following judgments: Dr. Shyam Bihari Gupta vs. The Rent Tribunal and Others, (2007) 1 RLW 262 (Rajasthan High Court decision) ; Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Premlata Shukla and Others, (2007) ACJ 1928; United India Insurance Company vs. Brijkishore Jatav and Another, 2011 (1) TAC 1015 (MP); Bijoy Kumar Dugar vs. Bidyadhar Dutta and Others, (2006) 2 ACC 36; Smt. Kalpana Devi Pandey and Others vs. Gabbar Singh Baghel and Others, 2010(2) TAC 996 (MP).
4.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimants contends that the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:904 3 MA-3351-2018 compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal was inadequate and should be enhanced.

The Claims Tribunal erred in assessing the deceased's monthly income at 60,617, pointing out that the salary statement exhibited by them (Exhibit P-55) indicates a salary of 62,638 in June, and given the recommendations of the Seventh Pay Commission, the salary should be taken as 90,000 per month.

The Claims Tribunal wrongly limited the compensation for loss of companionship, love, affection, care, and guidance to a meager 70,000,
considering the age of the claimants and their dependence on the deceased.
The compensation for these heads should be at least 10,00,000.

The Insurance Company's plea for contributory negligence, asserting that there was no specific pleading regarding the deceased's negligence, and the Claims Tribunal rightly held the driver of the Bolero pick-up responsible for the accident.

In support of their contentions, the claimants have relied on the following decisions:
Meera Devi and Another, 2014 ACJ 1012 ; Dinesh Kumar vs. National Insurance Company Limited and Others, 2018 ACJ 535 ; Shashikala and Others vs.
Gangalakshmamma and Another, 2015 ACJ 1239.
5.

sentences.text: The main issue is in regard to contributory negligence.

2 6.
The Insurance Company contends that the accident was due to the contributory negligence of the deceased.
It submits that the deceased was driving his vehicle rashly and on the wrong side of the road, thereby contributing to the head-on collision.

To support its case, the Insurance Company has adduced evidence from its investigator,
Surendra Singh Rajput (DW-1), who claims that the accident occurred due to the deceased's negligence.

On the other hand, the claimants argue that no specific plea regarding contributory negligence was taken by the Insurance Company before the Tribunal, and thus, it is not tenable to attribute negligence to the deceased.

The Tribunal, after considering the evidence, relied on the eye-witness testimony (PW-3)
and the spot map to conclude that the Bolero pick-up was primarily at fault for the accident.

Upon examining the evidence, this Court finds that while the Insurance NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:904 4 MA-3351-2018 Company raised the issue of contributory negligence, it failed to establish a clear factual basis for its claim.
The evidence provided by the investigator and other witnesses does not conclusively prove that the deceased was driving rashly or negligently.
The Tribunal's reliance on the spot map and the testimonies of the claimants' witnesses appears reasonable and is supported by the facts of the case.
Therefore, this Court concurs with the Tribunal's finding that the Bolero pick-up's driver was solely responsible for the accident.
In light of the above analysis, this Court finds no merit in the contentions raised by the Insurance Company regarding contributory negligence.
The evidence on record does not support the claim that the deceased was at fault for the accident.
The Claims Tribunal's finding that the accident was caused by the rash and negligent driving of the Bolero pick-up is upheld.
Accordingly, the misc. appeal filed by the Insurance Company stands dismissed.
7. The next question in regard to the enhancement of the compensation amount.

8. Learned counsel for the claimants submits that the monthly income of the deceased, Dr. Anil Kumar Dwivedi, has been clearly established based on documentary evidence submitted by the claimants, including salary statements, PAN card, and other supporting documents.

Mrs. Renu Dwivedi (PW1), the deceased's wife, testified that her husband was earning a total monthly income of 100,000 from his employment as a Senior Resident (SR) at the Medical College, Orai, and his additional work at the Samriddhi Clinic and on-call duties at other hospitals.

While it is acknowledged that Dr. Anil Kumar Dwivedi was employed as an SR at the Medical College with a salary of 60,617 per month as per Exhibit P-55 and P-56, it is also pertinent to note that he had additional sources of income, including private practice and on-call duties.

The claimants have submitted sufficient evidence in the form of the deceased's PAN card (Exhibit P-37), the clinic's registration (Exhibit P-40), and documents from Samriddhi Clinic, which clearly indicate that the deceased was engaged in private practice and earning additional income.
The bills for purchased medications also establish the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:904 5 MA-3351-2018 deceased's professional activities outside of his government employment.

The counsel submits that the Claims Tribunal should not ignore these additional sources of income while calculating the deceased's earnings, as it was well within his legal right to engage in private practice as a medical professional.

However, the Claims Tribunal has erroneously disregarded this and assessed the Smt. Renu vs Jagdish on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146692860/
3
deceased's income solely based on his salary from the Medical College.
The argument put forth by the Insurance Company, suggesting that the deceased could not have engaged in private practice due to the non- practicing allowance, is flawed and legally unsound.

The non-practicing allowance is meant to prevent private practice during the term of employment, but it does not eliminate the deceased's potential earnings from his private practice before or after the employment term.
9. On the other hand, learned Counsel for the Insurance Company opposed the contentions of learned Counsel for the claimants for the enhancement of the compensation amount.

10 It is true that in the case National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700, the Hon'ble Supreme Court, by a full bench of five judges, held that a 25 percent amount should be added to the income of a deceased person aged 40 to 50, who was self-employed or receiving a fixed salary, to account for the potential for future income growth.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. On perusal of the impugned award, it is found that the Claims Tribunal has erred in determining the deceased as a contract employee who was receiving a fixed salary and was found to be over 40 years of age.
Therefore, the deceased's annual income was added with 25 percent towards future prospects, resulting in 8,52,095.
Based on dependency, the deceased's annual income was certified to be 8,52,095.

However, in the present case, as per documents Ex.P.55 and P.56, it is clear that the deceased was posted as a Doctor at the Medical College, Jalaun, Orai, and was getting a salary with Dearness Allowance, which was regularly increased.
Thus, it appears that NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:904 6 MA-3351-2018 he was not a fixed-pay employee.

As regards loss of income, including future prospects, in the light of the judgment of the Apex Court,
the claimants are entitled to a loss of income, including future prospects, at 30%.

Similarly, the claimants are entitled to compensation towards consortium in the light of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Satinder Kaur @ Satinder Kaur Vs. Punjab State Road Transport Corporation [2020 SCC OnLine SC 305], wherein the Supreme Court observed that the amount for loss of consortium must be granted under the heads of loss of consortium, loss of estate, and funeral expenses, which should be in addition to the general compensation.

entities.text: Satinder Kaur @ Satinder Kaur Vs. Punjab State Road Transport Corporation [2020 SCC OnLine SC 305]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the claimants are entitled to get compensation under the following heads:-
HEAD AMOUNT Income 681,676 per annum (after deduction of income tax 50,000) After adding Future Prospects @ 30% 886,179 After adding Dependency 3/4 6,64,634 Multiplier (14) 93,04,876 Loss of Income 93,04,876

Other Heads:
Loss of Consortium 40,000 X 5 = 2,00,000 Loss of Estate and Funeral Expenses 30,000 Total Compensation 95,34,876 12.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is 95,34,876, as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of 90,17,000.

Accordingly,
the claimants are entitled to an additional sum of 5,17,876 over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.

Smt. Renu vs Jagdish on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146692860/
4 13.
In the result, this miscellaneous appeal filed by claimants is partly allowed, by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of 5,17,876.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization.
The enhanced amount shall be paid to the appellants within a period of three months from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this order.
The remaining conditions imposed by the Claims Tribunal shall remain unaltered.

If the enhanced amount of compensation exceeds the valuation of the appeal, the difference in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:904 7 MA-3351-2018 the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by claimants within a period of one month, and proof thereof shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
14. Both the miscellaneous appeals stand disposed of to the extent indicated above.
(HIRDESH) JUDGE MKB Smt. Renu vs Jagdish on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146692860/
